Connecting the ACCOUNT needs a browser (OAuth) - the token never passes through MCP or the CLI, and it is AES-encrypted at rest on the platform.
Org repos: the org must allow the Benmore OAuth app (GitHub → org settings → Third-party access). GitHub's error is surfaced verbatim on link.
Linking an EXISTING repo that already has unrelated commits will fail the first push as diverged - sync is one-way; use push --force to overwrite it with the platform history.

The mirror never forces on its own. When a failed feature_install, promote or refresh is rolled back after its commits were already mirrored, the next push is refused as diverged and the status shows it; the app owner decides whether to overwrite the remote with push --force (github_push force:true is owner-only).
An unpromoted app has no Live instance yet - only the dev branch pushes until the first promote.

Any editor can link an app that has no link, and change or unlink a link they made themselves; a link made by another member (typically the owner's mirror) can be replaced or removed only by the app owner, so an editor can't redirect the owner's commits to another repository.

Pushes use the token of the account that linked the app. If that account is removed from the app or drops below editor, the next push disables the sync with a visible reason instead of continuing; link again from an account that has access.

An ownership transfer switches the mirror off when it is accepted, unless the new owner is the one who linked it: the mirror pushes with the personal GitHub connection of whoever linked it, usually the previous owner, who stays on as an editor. github_status and the Version Control tab show it as paused with the reason; the accept result carries github_mirror_disabled and a notice. The repository on GitHub and the linker's GitHub connection are not touched. The new owner connects their own GitHub account and links a repository again (github_link); only the app owner can link or unlink a mirror a transfer switched off, so the member who made the link (still an editor) cannot switch it back on.
